To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a low molecular weight factor in the mucosa from the small intestine of the cow stimulates DNA synthesis in rat primary cultured hepatocytes and in vivo hepatocyte proliferation in the regenerating liver.

a factor with a molecular mass of less than 1000 in the bovine small-intestinal mucosa (low molecular weight or LMW factor), stimulates hepatocyte proliferation in rat primary culture, and in vivo after partial hepatectomy.

the LMW factor stimulates DNA synthesis in hepatocytes in primary cultures and in vivo, but it only shows its action when it is added with the HMW factor, and that the HMW factor might be a hepatotrophic factor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of a hepatotrophin from the bovine mucosa of the small intestine.
the identification and purification of a hepatotrophin that is present in the mucosa from the small intestine of the bovine.
the effects of the LMW and HMW factors, which are found in the bovine small mucosa, on hepatocyte proliferation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LMW factor is one of the components of the hepatotrophic growth factors that act synergistically with other growth factors to stimulate hepatocyte proliferation in vivo.
the LMW factor in the small intestinal mucosa might be one of the factors that enhance hepatocyte proliferation in the liver.
the LMW factor is one of the hepatotrophic factors in the bovine small-intestinal mucosa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a LMW factor in the bovine small intestines acts synergistically with a hepatotrophic factor(s), which is provided in the liver, to stimulate hepatocyte proliferation.
the LMW factor is a new hepatotrophic growth stimulant and that the HMW factor is the factor that acts synergistically with it.
the LMW factor is a new factor with hepatotrophic activity, which is a component of the HMW fraction and acts synergistically with hepatotrophic growth factors such as EGF and HGH.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the small intestinal mucosa is a source of a factor that stimulates hepatocyte proliferation, and this factor may be involved in the control of liver growth.
the LMW factor in bovine intestinal mucosa is a novel hepatotrophic growth stimulator that can enhance hepatocyte proliferation in primary culture and in vivo.
the LMW factor stimulates hepatocyte proliferation, and the HMW factor enhances the activity of the LMW factors.
